content: It'd better if you could consider setting the status of your contribution to WIP to allow for a proper review and necessary adjustments before opening it for approval by others. I haven't read the statement in detail or done any play-testing yet. The following points are based on a quick initial scan: Rules * Please limit formatting to the variable names only, excluding other characters such as brackets, commas, equality signs and numbers. Victory Conditions and Defeat Conditions * These sections are missing. Please refer to other bot game contributions for the standard HTML code to use. Initialization Input / Input for One Game Turn * All lines: Please specify the format and variable types (e.g. 3 space-separated integers, or an integer). * Please format all line numbers using the "" tag. Output for One Game Turn * Please change "Output one line per owned drone" to "One line per owned drone". Thanks.

Thank you for your kind words in the comment on Chrono-Tactics. I'm happy to see similar updates have been applied to Quantum and Corsairs, so I won't have to repeat myself, which is great😆

As I plan to review all three contributions' statements before doing any play-testing, I'll leave Chrono-Tactics aside for now and return to it later.

Onto the comments on this contribution:

Turn Resolution Order
* Drone Movement

  - Please specify that movement is in a straight line and that drones and Pulsars never collide (if my understanding is correct).

  - Can drones, whether on the same or opposing teams, and/or Pulsars occupy the same coordinates?

* Laser Relay Links

  - Please clarify whether laser beams are straight lines. This is important for determining whether beams intersect and interfere with each other.

  - Please clarify whether a valid link lasts only for the turn in which LINK is issued, it persists across subsequent turns until the drone moves out of range of the target.

  - Can drones on the same team link to the same target?

* Quantum Beam Interference

  - In "Normal vs Normal (or Overcharged vs Overcharged)", please remove the brackets and add a comma before "or".

  - Please change "Overcharged beam retains 6 bandwidth" to "Overcharged beam's bandwidth is halved to 6".

* Energy Harvesting & Flow

  - If drones from opposing teams are both within 200 units of the same Pulsar, do they harvest energy simultaneously, subject to their respective bandwidths? If so, what happens when the Pulsar's remaining energy is less than their combined bandwidth?

  - "Pulsars regenerate 3 to 5 energy": Please clarify whether each Pulsar has a fixed energy regeneration rate that differs between Pulsars.

General gameplay
* I played a random game between two copies of the default AI bot in Wood 1. My impression was that, once the drones had been positioned and the required relay paths established, they could simply remain in place until the game ended, with little need to interact with the opponent.

  - The distances between Pulsars, combined with the limited number of drones, seem to result in players establishing relay paths that rarely intersect with their opponent's paths, making quantum beam interference less relevant.

  - Pulsar energy doesn't seem to run out, so there's little incentive to redeploy drones to other locations.

  - Giving different Pulsars different energy regeneration characteristics could make the game more interesting. For example, some could start with less/more energy but have a higher/lower, more/less stable (narrower/wider-range) regeneration rate. (The default stub comment describes Pulsar energy as unstable. Perhaps this refers to some physical property, but the quantity itself feels pretty stable to me.)

  I may have formed the wrong impression from observing just one game. What do you think?

Input for One Game Turn
* Consider including each Pulsar's energy regeneration rate in the turn input.

Thanks again
